To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The reaction of cytochrome C peroxidase with hydrogen peroxide occurs via a two-step mechanism, and (2) The first step of the reaction is the protonation of a distal histidine residue.

the mutation of His-52 to Leu in the distal heme site of cytochrome C peroxidase causes a large decrease in reactivity with peroxides, that the mutation causes a significant structural change in the active site, but that the structural changes are not the cause of the loss of reacitivity.

the reaction of H2O2 with the H52L mutant of CcP(Mi) has a rate constant of approximately 1/10,000 of the wild-type enzyme, that the rate is pH dependent in a manner that is consistent with protonation of the distal His residue, and that the reaction mechanism involves the protonation of the peroxide oxygen atom.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the active-site histidines in the reaction of cytochrome C peroxidase with peroxide.
the mechanism and structure of cytochrome C peroxidase.
the mechanism and kinetics of the reaction of cytochrome C peroxidase with hydrogen peroxide and the role of the distal heme ligand in this reaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the distal His is a critical residue in the rapid formation of compound I.

the distal histidine is critical for rapid formation of the enzyme compound I and that the mutation causes a loss of reactivty with hydrogen peroxide that can be attributed to a loss of the protonation state of the distal histidyl residue.

the distal histidine of cytochrome P450 (His-52), is essential for the formation of compound I, and that the loss of reactivities of the H52 mutant is caused by a combination of the loss of the distal histidyl ligand and the loss of the proximal histidyl ligands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
His-52 is a critical amino acid for the formation of compound I in cytochrome c peroxydase.
the distal histidine in CcP is a key residue in the formation of compound I and that this role is due to the ability of the distal histidyl group to stabilize the ferryl oxygen.

the mutation causes a 10(6)-fold decrease in the reactivity of the enzyme with peroxide, but the residual reactivity of H52L is pH-dependent and is consistent with a protonation event at a group with a pKa of 4.5.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distal histidine plays a key role in the formation of the active compound I intermediate.
the mutation of His52 to Leu in CcP(Mi) has two effects on the enzyme's reactivity with hydrogen-peroxide.
the distal histidine is a critical residue in cytochrome c peroixdase (CCP) for rapid formation of the compound I intermediate.
